newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: N Korea says UN should stop providing cover for US.
newsitem.headline: N Korea says UN should stop providing cover for US.

text.p: North Korea's deputy foreign minister on Thursday lashed out at Japan and told the United Nations it should remove its name from U.S. troops responsible for armistice arrangements between the two Koreas.

Choi Su Hon told the General Assembly Japan was colluding militarily with the United States against North Korea. He also said Japan did not deserve a permanent Security Council seat because it had not properly apologised and compensated its Second World War victims.

"Japan is attempting to become a permanent member (of the council) while having failed to make an apology and compensation for the war crimes in a right manner ... but instead justifying them," he said. "This is a mockery of the U.N. member states, particularly Asian countries."
Japan and Germany are pushing for permanent council seats. Discussion of expanding the 15-member body has been underway for two years but disagreements persist on who should join.
Choi did not refer to a North Korean submarine that ran aground off South Korea last week, setting off a manhunt as South Korean security forces tracked down its crew.

He again appealed to the United States to conclude a new peace agreement to replace the 1953 armistice, a proposal that Washington has rejected, calling instead for four-party peace talks that would include South Korea and China.
In the meantime, Choi said, the United Nations should "without delay" remove its name and flag from U.S. troops in South Korea in an effort to aid new peace arrangements.
"The existence of the U.N. Command in South Korea constitutes a legal obstacle to turning the state of armistice into durable peace and termining the Cold War on the Korean peninsula," he said.
He said the U.N. command was a product of the Cold War era that came into existence "through the abuse of the name of the United Nations" and that only U.S. troops remain there today.
The Security Council on June 27, 1950 adopted a resolution naming the United States as head of a military command to repulse North Korea's attacks on the south.
Choi said the United States, Japan and South Korea were attempting to build up a "tripartite military alliance' by launching joint military exercises.

"Particularly, the arms race is further accelerated because the Japanese authorities are resorting to the unreasonable policy of becoming a military superpower," he said. "We strongly urge the Japanese authorities to end their confrontation acts against (North Korea) such as arms buildup under the veil of the 'immediate response in case of emergency.'"
